plan.summary: BRO-4623 part 5: Betrayal (2013, Daniel Craig/Rachel Weisz) carried the Rebecca musical's investor-fraud story, its sources and a Flop label; The Hollywood Reporter reports it recouped about ten weeks into its 14-week run. Also removes false statements from the notes of MJ, The Music Man, The Outsiders, Stranger Things and Operation Mincemeat.
steps: Betrayal: THR 'Betrayal Concludes Smash Broadway Run' (Jan 2014): $17.5M cumulative gross, recouped roughly ten weeks in, budget not disclosed. Deadline (Dec 2013): $1.44M week, a record for a play.
MJ: recoupedDate 2023-05 (16 months after opening); the note's 'Recouped Nov 2023' contradicted it.
The Music Man closed Jan 15, 2023, not Jan 2024.
The Outsiders: Stranger Things has not recouped, so 'first new musical to recoup since Stranger Things' is false.
Stranger Things: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child and Spider-Man cost more; 'largest Broadway capitalization on record' is false.
Operation Mincemeat: extended through Mar 14, 2027 (10th extension), not Feb 2026.

actions.newValue: The Hollywood Reporter (Jan 2014): recouped roughly ten weeks into its 14-week limited run; budget not disclosed.

actions.oldValue: Initial budget mentioned as $12 million before fraud inflated it to $16 million
Broadway production was cancelled due to investor fraud scandal. Initial $12M budget inflated to $16M due to fraud. Show never opened on Broadway despite years of development.
actions.newValue: Mike Nichols' revival of Harold Pinter's play with Daniel Craig, Rachel Weisz and Rafe Spall at the Ethel Barrymore, Oct 2013 to Jan 5, 2014 (14-week limited run). Grossed just over $17.5M and set a record for a play with a $1.44M week. Recouped about ten weeks into the run (The Hollywood Reporter); capitalization not disclosed.

actions.oldValue: Recouped in ~16 months. Received $10M SVOG grant. Has grossed over $200M. National tour also profitable. Note: Jackson Estate receives 100% of producer profit share — actual investor returns depend on estate's profit participation terms, which are not publicly disclosed. Weekly cost ~$1.3M. Recouped Nov 2023. $10M SVOG grant. Jackson Estate negotiated 100% of lead-producer profits + 13% off-the-top after recoup+10%.
actions.newValue: Recouped about 16 months after opening (May 2023). Received a $10M SVOG grant. Has grossed over $200M. Weekly cost about $1.3M. The Michael Jackson estate negotiated 100% of lead-producer profits plus 13% off the top after recoupment plus 10%, so investor returns depend on terms that are not public.

actions.oldValue: Star-driven revival with Hugh Jackman and Sutton Foster that opened Feb 2022. Capitalized at ~$24M with ~$1M weekly running costs. Despite strong grosses (regularly $2-3M/week, $187.8M total over 374 performances), the extremely high capitalization and running costs meant it came close but likely did not fully recoup before closing Jan 2024.
actions.newValue: Star-driven revival with Hugh Jackman and Sutton Foster that opened Feb 2022 and closed Jan 15, 2023. Capitalized at about $24M with about $1M weekly running costs. Grossed $2-3M a week ($187.8M over 374 performances), but no recoupment was announced before closing.

actions.oldValue: Won Best Musical Tony 2024. Recouped $22M investment week ending December 28, 2025 after 744 performances (89 weeks) and $121M+ total grosses. First new musical to recoup since Stranger Things (2022). Actors from developmental workshops entitled to profit-sharing per NYT.
actions.newValue: Won the 2024 Tony for Best Musical. Recouped its $22M investment in the week ending Dec 28, 2025, after 744 performances (89 weeks) and $121M+ in grosses. Actors from developmental workshops are entitled to profit-sharing (NYT).

actions.oldValue: Netflix/Sonia Friedman production. Won 4 Tony Awards 2025. SEC Form D shows $29M-$31.5M capitalization ('Now A Warning LLC' — largest Broadway capitalization on record). Being filmed Feb 2026 for future release.
actions.newValue: Netflix/Sonia Friedman production; won 4 Tony Awards in 2025. SEC Form D (Now A Warning LLC) shows a $29M-$31.5M capitalization. Closing Jan 3, 2027 with no recoupment announced.

actions.oldValue: West End hit transferred to Broadway. Weekly costs $500K vs London's £100K. Break-even ~$600K weekly but averaging $580K - running below break-even. Extended through Feb 2026 on strong word-of-mouth despite soft grosses. [Merged from duplicate operation-mincemeat-2025 entry: Broadway transfer from London (originally capitalized at £2 million). Reports indicate show needs to average $146/ticket for a year to recoup, and at current pace would not recoup until 2028. Show is not losing money but faces long path to profitability.]
actions.newValue: West End hit transferred to Broadway (opened Mar 20, 2025; extended through Mar 14, 2027). Weekly costs about $500K against a break-even near $600K. BroadwayWorld reported that at its pace it would not recoup until about 2028; no recoupment announced.
